notes:
I couldn't do this research, so there are no commentary notes yet.

My first batch of searches was blocked with the message that I had "no more code_execution tool calls remaining this turn." I tried twice more. One search did run, but it came back in a form I couldn't read, and the last attempt was blocked the same way. I didn't open a single page on any of your approved sites.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say and give a URL for each point. Writing notes on Daniel 2:25–49 from memory would break that rule, so I've left them out.

**What I'll do when the tools work again (for example, if you send the request again):**

1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word on Daniel 2; the Bible Hub and StudyLight pages for Gill, Ellicott, Barnes and the Pulpit Commentary on vv. 25–49; Precept Austin's Daniel 2 page; Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu); Calvin on Daniel (ccel.org).
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** I expect most of the disagreement to be in vv. 40–45. That covers the fourth kingdom, the iron-and-clay feet and toes, and when and how the stone strikes. The questions are whether the stone's kingdom came at Christ's first coming and the church, or will come at his return, and whether there's a "revived Roman Empire." I'd look for each view on its own tradition's sites: Reformed and amillennial (Ligonier, The Gospel Coalition, Monergism), dispensational and Baptist (GTY, Desiring God, Got Questions), Wesleyan (Seedbed, Wesley), Pentecostal (Enduring Word, AG), and Lutheran (LCMS, 1517).
3. **Other views:** Bible Odyssey and the NET Bible notes for the scholarly view that the kingdoms run Babylon, Media, Persia and Greece. For Catholic and Orthodox readings, New Advent (including Jerome's commentary on Daniel), Catholic.com and OCA, especially on the stone "cut out without hands" (vv. 34, 45). I'd also check for any notable popular modern teaching on Daniel's promotion and gifts (vv. 46–49), and include it only if those sites actually discuss it.
